Slow-Smoked Baby Back Ribs

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 4 hours

Slow-smoked baby back ribs are a hearty and flavorful dish often served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This feast commemorates the biblical story of the Holy Innocents, and the rich, comforting ribs symbolize warmth and community during this solemn yet celebratory occasion.

Ingredients

  • 2 racks baby back ribs (about 3 pounds / 1.4 kg each)
  • 1/4 cup brown sugar (50 g)
  • 2 tablespoons smoked paprika
  • 1 tablespoon garlic powder
  • 1 tablespoon onion powder
  • 1 tablespoon kosher salt
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
  • 1/2 cup apple juice (120 ml)
  • 1/2 cup barbecue sauce (120 ml), for glazing
  • Wood chips for smoking (hickory or applewood preferred)

Method

  1. Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs for better smoke penetration.
  2. In a bowl, combine brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, kosher salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper to make the dry rub.
  3. Generously coat both sides of the ribs with the dry rub, pressing it into the meat.
  4. Preheat your smoker to 225°F (107°C) and add wood chips according to the manufacturer's instructions.
  5. Place the ribs bone side down on the smoker rack and smoke for 3 hours, maintaining a steady temperature.
  6. After 3 hours, wrap the ribs tightly in aluminum foil with the apple juice inside to keep them moist.
  7. Return the wrapped ribs to the smoker and cook for an additional 1 hour.
  8. Carefully remove the ribs from foil and brush them with barbecue sauce.
  9. Place the ribs back on the smoker for 15-30 minutes to set the glaze and develop a sticky finish.
  10. Remove from smoker, let rest for 10 minutes, then slice between the bones and serve.

Tips

  • Soak wood chips in water for at least 30 minutes before smoking to create flavorful smoke.
  • For a spicier kick, increase cayenne pepper or add chili powder to the rub.
  • If you don't have a smoker, you can cook the ribs low and slow in the oven at 225°F (107°C) and finish under the broiler with barbecue sauce.
